<reason>B wins by distinguishing sustained restrictive disinflation from abandoning the target and requiring faster adjustment to justify its additional unemployment costs. A identifies a legitimate entrenchment risk but repeatedly treats a larger future recession as guaranteed and an immediate recession as bounded without establishing either. B answers the operational credibility challenge and exposes the uneven treatment of lasting economic damage. A’s concession that falling inflation and anchored expectations need not warrant recession further strengthens B’s central comparison.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B explains that firms can distinguish gradualism from surrender through observable disinflation, continued restraint, and conditional tightening. When A attacks the proposed trigger as necessarily waiting two quarters, B correctly identifies its explicit early-action provision. A repeats that misreading in closing rather than resolving the rebuttal.</best_rebuttal>
